Consistent with Geoff Crossley's 607 Elmira exchange.

color.$note: Read by eye off the supplied Ferrario Ford artwork on 30 Sep 2026, not sampled from a brand sheet and not pulled from a stylesheet, so treat these as close rather than exact and confirm the hex values before the first send. The same caveat is on Bob Johnson's palette for the same reason. What matters more than the exact hex is that the previous values were wrong in kind, not just in degree: they were a guessed Ford corporate blue, and this brand is a deep navy ground with a RED wordmark. Accent drives every button and rule in the email, so a blue accent would have shipped a red brand's campaign in the wrong colour entirely.
color.accentDarkNote: Exists only because the mid-tone red at 9px on white does not have the contrast to read. Used for small legal and eyebrow type, never for a button ground.

logo.$note:
Two lockups were supplied and they are not interchangeable. See dealer.storeNote for which business each one is. This file uses the Ferrario Ford rooftop mark.

useImage stays false, and the artwork does not change that. A hosted image does not render when the client blocks images, which is a large share of opens, so the header carries a type lockup we control. That is the same call as Bob Johnson and the same call build.mjs already makes for DriveOne's own D mark.

Two parts of the rooftop mark are deliberately not reproduced. The white cowboy hat resting on the final O is a drawn element with no type equivalent, the same problem as the D mark. The Ford oval is omitted for a different and more important reason: this email sells a DriveOne VSC administered by Ascent and, in New York, obligated by ORIAS. Ford is not the administrator, the obligor or the seller, and setting their oval beside the offer implies a manufacturer endorsement that does not exist. brand/offer.json is strict about not making claims the contract does not support; this is that same rule applied to artwork. If someone wants the oval in the header, that is a question for Ford's trademark guidelines and the client's Ford rep, not a build setting.
logo.lightNote: The partner record's logo, still unopened from this environment. Now that the client has supplied artwork directly, check whether this stored file is the rooftop mark or the group mark before any future switch to useImage true.

wordmark.$note: CONFIRMED against the supplied rooftop artwork: FERRARIO is set in a heavy italic, which is what italic true reproduces. line2 is FORD because this is the Ford rooftop; the group lockup would read AUTO TEAM instead. The rule under the wordmark is always color.accent, never set here, so the two cannot drift apart.

contact.addressNote: CONFIRMED 1 Oct 2026 by two independent sources that agree: Ferrario Ford's own website Find Us panel, and the Google Business Profile for Ferrario Auto Team. The site gives ZIP+4 as 14903-1044; the footer prints the five digit form, which is what CAN-SPAM needs and what a reader expects. A physical postal address in the footer is a legal requirement, not a nicety, and this one is now satisfied.
contact.phoneNote:
USABLE BUT NOT IDEAL, and deliberately not left blocking. This is the main dealership number from the Ferrario Auto Team Google Business Profile, so it is genuinely customer facing and a caller reaches the dealership and gets routed. It is NOT confirmed to be the service department's direct line, and Ryan said the dealership would say which number they want printed. Swap it when they do.

What it is definitely better than: 607-526-7748, which is Geoff Crossley's number on the partner record and is the PROGRAM contact rather than a customer service line. Bob Johnson made the same distinction. Never print the program contact's number in a customer footer.
contact.replyToNote:
SET 1 Oct 2026. Lowercased from the way it was given; Workspace treats the local part as case insensitive, and keeping one casing avoids a mismatch later when something compares strings.

A real monitored mailbox that already exists and already receives mail, chosen over a Google Group and over a forwarding service on ferrario.driveoneprogram.com. Both of those are better on paper and neither was worth blocking the launch for. The upgrade path is open and changes nothing a customer sees.

TWO THINGS THIS MAILBOX OWES THE CAMPAIGN, until auto-suppression is built:
  1. Any reply that reads as an opt-out must reach vsc_suppression. Nothing in the system      reads replies today. Workflow 03 handles Resend webhooks only: bounces, complaints and      the one-click unsubscribe. A customer who types 'take me off this list' is invisible to      the campaign and will receive all ten emails. CAN-SPAM wants it honoured within 10      business days however it is expressed.
  2. Real questions should reach the dealership. The emails are written as though the service      drive sent them, so a customer asking about their own vehicle is owed an answer from      Ferrario rather than from DriveOne.

Note the From address, service@ferrario.driveoneprogram.com, still cannot receive mail: that subdomain has no MX, no A and no CNAME. Clients and auto-responders that reply to From rather than Reply-To will hard bounce. Not a launch blocker, and fixed by putting a forwarder on the subdomain whenever that is worth doing.

campaign.quoteUrlBaseNote:
PREVIEW ONLY. This value is read by email/build.mjs when it renders the local dist and preview HTML, and by nothing else. A production send never uses it: the scheduler reads vsc_enrollment.quote_url, which workflow 05 fills with the guided_purchase_link returned by the quote API, and refuses to send at all while that column is null (n8n/build-workflows.mjs, the quote_url is not null guard). Templates in vsc_email_template carry the {{quote_url}} merge tag, not this string.

It previously read "SET VIA SHORT_LINK_BASE_URL IN n8n", which was wrong twice over: no workflow reads a SHORT_LINK_BASE_URL variable, and docs/SUPABASE.md says plainly that no link is ever built locally. That placeholder is where the phantom fifth n8n variable came from.
campaign.unsubscribeNote: Same deployed Supabase Edge Function as Bob Johnson. It is keyed per recipient and scoped by dealer_id in the URL, so dealerships share it without touching each other's opt outs. Set both UNSUBSCRIBE_URL_BASE and PREFERENCES_URL_BASE to this.
campaign.idNote: Distinct from Bob Johnson on purpose. vsc_enrollment and vsc_email_template are keyed on (dealer_id, campaign_id, ...), so a shared id would put two dealerships in one campaign namespace.

staffEmailDomains: NEEDS CONFIRMATION: the dealership mail domain, probably ferrarioford.com
intake.$comment:
NEW 5 Oct 2026, fixing a fork carryover. Ferrario inherited Bob Johnson's exclusion list: it filtered bob johnson, widrick and caprara, which are Rochester-area names that do not occur in Elmira service data, and it filtered @bobjohnsonauto.com while leaving Ferrario's own domain eligible. So the two filters that matter here were both pointed at the wrong dealership.

internalNames now catches Ferrario's own records, which is the common case: the Auto Team group's other rooftops and internal entries written under the store name.

staffEmailDomains is UNCONFIRMED and deliberately not blocking. While it carries a marker the engine emits no staff filter at all and says so in a SQL comment, which is the honest failure: a guessed domain would look like a working filter and exclude nobody. Fill it in and the predicate appears on the next build. The risk while it is empty is small and bounded - a staff member is only eligible if they personally had a service-drive quote created, and the opening cohort is 30 - but it is a real risk and worth one line from the dealership.

Local competitors who took a trade belong here too, as and when the store names them. That was two of the first thirteen bad rows at Bob Johnson.

supabase.$comment: CONFIRMED. partners.id here equals dealers.source_id in MetricBridge, which is the join between the two systems.
supabase.partner_type_note: Note this is NOT 'service-drive' as on Bob Johnson. Do not copy that value across.
supabase.cohort_target_note:
DECISION 6 Oct 2026, by Ryan: market to the WHOLE No Warranty Bucket, not a 350 person slice of it. That supersedes the earlier 350 target.

1,098 is measured, not the 1,244 quoted elsewhere in this file. 1,244 is the raw count of has_existing_warranty = false; 1,098 is how many distinct PEOPLE survive every intake filter (90 day window, pending quote, contactable, not suppressed, not internal, not a junk address, mileage and model year present, one row per person rather than per visit). The gap is mostly customers with more than one visit in the window plus the excluded rows. Re-measure rather than assuming: the number moves as new service visits land.

THE TARGET IS THE AUDIENCE. THE RAMP IS THE SCHEDULE. They are different decisions and this file keeps them in different fields. initial_cohort is where the ramp has got to; cohort_target is where it is going. Raising initial_cohort is the only thing that enrols anybody.
supabase.initial_cohort_note:
RAMP STEP 1 OF 6, set 1 Oct 2026, target revised to the full 1,098 on 6 Oct.

Raise it in steps, watching bounce and complaint rates at each one before taking the next:
  step 1    30     single digits to about 20 a day
  step 2    90     about 30 to 50 a day
  step 3    200    about 60 to 100 a day
  step 4    350    peak near 200, the old target
  step 5    650    REQUIRES dailyCap above 200, see sending.dailyCapNote
  step 6    1098   full bucket, every eligible customer

Opening at the full number starts enormous on day one. ferrario.driveoneprogram.com is a brand new subdomain with a brand new DKIM key on Amazon SES IPs it has never sent from, so day one is the worst possible moment for the largest volume. The parent domain's reputation helps; it does not substitute for a ramp.

This value is a ceiling on TOTAL enrolment, not per run. Raising it IS the ramp: the hourly sweep tops up to the new number and then enrols nobody until it is raised again. Check the shape at any step with: node scripts/simulate-volume.mjs ferrario-ford

Steps 5 and 6 do not fit under a 200 a day cap. 1,098 people is 10,980 sends; at 200 a day across 4 send days a week that is about 14 weeks pinned at the ceiling, and because the scheduler defers whatever it cannot send, every contact's 60 day sequence stretches well past 60 days. Nothing errors and nothing double sends - the cadence just quietly stops being the cadence. Raise dailyCap to about 300 before step 5, or accept the stretch deliberately.

UNTIL THE FIX OF 6 OCT 2026 RAISING THIS NUMBER DID NOT WORK. The intake limit was spent on customers already enrolled, so 30 -> 90 enrolled 31 people rather than 60 and the sweep after that enrolled nobody, for good. See the comments on the limit in n8n/build-workflows.mjs and the 'a raised cohort actually fills' check in n8n/verify.mjs. Any ramp step taken before that fix under-delivered; re-check the enrolment count against this number after every raise rather than assuming the sweep did what it was told.
supabase.intake_window_note: Their quotes run 30 Apr to 14 Sep 2026, and 1,222 of the 1,244 fall inside 90 days, so a 90 day window captures effectively the whole list. Only 33 are inside 30 days, so a 30 day window would strand 97% of it.
supabase.max_mileage_note: Effectively off, same as Bob Johnson. The rating API is keyed on VIN and decides what it can rate; a local ceiling only second guesses it, and a vehicle it cannot price records a pricing_error, never sends, and stops being retried after five attempts.
supabase.data_quality_flag: RESOLVED 30 Sep 2026, decision by Ryan: market to the has_existing_warranty = false group. Checked before accepting it. The column is fully populated at both stores, zero nulls, so it IS being written for Ferrario rather than missing: 1 true and 1,243 false, against Bob Johnson's 37 and 410. Payment status could not corroborate either way because every quote at both rooftops is still 'pending', so nobody has bought yet anywhere. The rate difference between the two stores is a dealership-reality question rather than a data one.
supabase.data_quality_residual_risk: Worth holding in mind rather than acting on: this flag is the ONLY guard against pitching coverage to someone who already owns it. The rating API will happily quote an existing owner because it has no idea they have a contract, and intake filters on nothing else. So if Ferrario under-reports the flag, those customers receive the campaign. At Bob Johnson's 8.3% rate that would be roughly 100 people of 1,244. The filter itself is written as `= false`, which excludes nulls as well as trues, so an unknown is treated as ineligible. That is the safe direction.

brandLead.$comment: dealer means the dealership colour leads the layout and DriveOne is reduced to the provider mark in the header. Correct for a send made on their behalf.

sending.$comment: Copied from Bob Johnson deliberately. These are starting heuristics rather than measured truths, and the two stores are close enough in audience that starting from the same numbers is more honest than inventing different ones.
sending.dailyCapNote:
Hard ceiling per calendar day in dealer local time, enforced inside the atomic claim so two scheduler runs cannot jointly exceed it.

200 is sized for a cohort of about 350. It does NOT fit the full 1,098 person bucket that supabase.cohort_target now commits to: 10,980 sends at 200 a day over 4 send days a week is about 14 weeks at the ceiling, and the overflow does not queue neatly - it defers each contact's next step, so the 60 day cadence stretches. Raise this to roughly 300 before taking the cohort past 350, and only once the subdomain has a few weeks of clean bounce and complaint numbers behind it. Raising the cap on a cold domain is the one change that can cost deliverability outright.
sending.daysNote: Tuesday through Friday. Monday is excluded because Monday inboxes are cleared in bulk. Friday is INCLUDED for an arithmetic reason rather than a preference: two days drawn from Tue/Wed/Thu alone can only ever be 1, 2, 5, 6 or 7 days apart, so the 3 and 4 day gaps the deck opens with are impossible to express and every gap silently collapses to 7. Do not narrow this without re-running n8n/verify.mjs.
sending.hoursNote: Local. Mid morning and early afternoon, skipping the lunch hour.
sending.maxPerRunNote: Ceiling on any single hourly run, so a backlog cannot arrive as one spike.
sending.fromNote:
DECIDED 1 Oct 2026: send on a per-dealer subdomain of a DriveOne root, not on the dealership's own domain and not on a Kovara domain.

Why a DriveOne root. Ferrario's sending mailbox turned out to live on Captured's server, which nobody can reach. The Kovara domains were offered as warm alternatives and rejected: they are the dealer-acquisition cold prospecting stack, and copy that says 'the service department you drove to' cannot ship from getkovara.com.

Why a SUBDOMAIN and not the root. driveoneprogram.com is a live Google Workspace domain carrying real people's mailboxes. Putting 3,500 consumer sends on the root would do to DriveOne's own corporate mail exactly what sending from ferrario.com risked doing to the dealership's. The subdomain also leaves the root SPF untouched, which matters because a domain gets exactly one.

Why PER DEALER. Reputation then fails per rooftop, the same way dist, workflows and campaign ids already separate per rooftop. A complaint spike at one dealership does not reach another's customers. It also puts the dealership's name in the visible From domain, which is the next best thing to sending from their own.

The root is one field to change if the client prefers driveonepartners.com or driveonedealers.com; all three are on Vercel DNS with the same Google MX, the same `~all` SPF and the same `p=none` DMARC, so the setup is identical. Do NOT use driveonedirect.com, which is the DTC money site, or driveonenow.com, which has no MX at all.

n8n's SEND_FROM must read `fromName <fromAddress>` and is checked at launch.
